title: Wire shellcheck into CI and triage the 29 SC2034 findings in the e2e harness
description:
Four tracked .sh files have NO static analysis of any kind. Neither biome nor tsc can give
them any -- LCLI-486 closed the .mjs/.cjs half of this hole and could not close this one, and
named it in tsconfig.scripts.json's header as a deliberate gap rather than leaving it to be
rediscovered.

MEASURED 2026-09-14 with shellcheck 0.11.0 at -S warning, 31 findings across 4 files:

  docker/e2e/lib/steps.sh        1   SC2148 (error) no shebang -- it is a SOURCED library,
                                     so the fix is a `# shellcheck shell=bash` directive
  docker/e2e/run-e2e.sh         29   ALL SC2034 "appears unused"
  docker/e2e/selftest.sh         0   clean
  scripts/publish-release.sh     0   clean as of LCLI-486 (its one SC2088 was a false
                                     positive -- a display label, never used as a path --
                                     and now carries a disable directive giving that reason)

THE 29 ARE THE POINT AND THEY NEED INDIVIDUAL TRIAGE, NOT A BULK SUPPRESSION. SC2034 is the
shell equivalent of the exact defect that motivated LCLI-486: an unused top-level constant
that shipped green because nothing looked. Some will be genuine false positives (shellcheck
cannot see indirect use), but several look like CAPTURED BASELINES THAT ARE NEVER COMPARED,
which would mean an assertion that does not assert -- an e2e check that has been passing by
doing nothing. Worth opening first:

  run-e2e.sh:250   LCLI298_AGENTS_BASELINE_HASH = "$(sha256sum AGENTS.md)"
  run-e2e.sh:263   CODEX_BRIDGE_HASH_BEFORE  \  a before/after pair where neither side
  run-e2e.sh:269   CODEX_BRIDGE_HASH_AFTER   /  appears to be compared
  run-e2e.sh:1077  BEFORE_INDEX / :1081 AFTER_INDEX        same shape
  run-e2e.sh:472   TASK1_TITLE_FILE_BEFORE / :476 _AFTER   same shape

A `*_RC` variable captured and never checked is the same hazard: the command's exit code was
recorded and then never asserted on. There are at least eleven of those.

DO NOT bulk-add `# shellcheck disable=SC2034`. That converts a real signal into permanent
silence and is WORSE than today, because it looks like the question was answered. Each finding
gets exactly one of: the assertion it was always meant to have, deletion of a dead capture, or
a disable directive NAMING why the use is indirect.

SCOPE
- Add shellcheck to CI over every tracked .sh, at a severity decided here and recorded.
  Ubuntu runners ship it preinstalled; confirm rather than assume.
- Add `npm run lint:shell` (or equivalent) so the same check is runnable locally by the same
  command CI uses -- a gate only reachable in CI is one nobody runs before pushing.
- Fix steps.sh's SC2148 with a shell directive, not a shebang; it is sourced, not executed.
- Triage all 29 SC2034 individually, per the rule above.
- Decide whether CODEX_BRIDGE_* should exist at all. Codex is retired as an agent runtime for
  this fleet, but `lore init --codex` remains a shipped PRODUCT SURFACE, so the harness may
  legitimately still exercise it. Decide deliberately; do not delete on the retirement alone.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: docker/e2e/run-e2e.sh is the "docker e2e harness (real lore
+ backlog binaries)" job, which is one of only THREE required status checks on dev. If some of
its assertions are inert, a required gate is measuring less than it appears to -- the same
class of problem as a required check naming a job that no longer runs.

acceptanceCriteria.text: shellcheck runs in CI over every tracked .sh file, and the identical check is runnable locally through a documented npm script

All 29 SC2034 findings in docker/e2e/run-e2e.sh are triaged INDIVIDUALLY -- each gets the missing assertion, deletion of a dead capture, or a disable directive naming why the use is indirect. No bulk suppression.

Any capture that turns out never to have been compared is REPORTED as a finding about the e2e harness rather than silently deleted, because it means a required check was asserting less than it appeared to
docker/e2e/lib/steps.sh's SC2148 is fixed with a `shellcheck shell=bash` directive rather than a shebang, since the file is sourced rather than executed
A planted unused variable in a tracked .sh fails the new CI check -- verified by planting it, not assumed

finalSummary:
DELIVERED in PR #54, CI run 34874684139 on that PR's own head (d787cd7c), all jobs green.

THE ALARMING PREMISE OF THIS TASK WAS DISPROVEN, and I wrote that premise, so the correction
leads. This record claimed several of the 29 SC2034 "appears unused" findings looked like
CAPTURED BASELINES NEVER COMPARED -- assertions that do not assert, inside a job that is one
of only three required checks on dev. The orchestrator raised the priority on that basis.

It is not what is happening. 28 of the 29 are ONE mechanical false positive. Assertions in
run-e2e.sh are written `check "<name>" '<expr>'` and check() runs `eval "$expr"`
(docker/e2e/lib/steps.sh:144-146). The expression is SINGLE-quoted so it evaluates at
assertion time rather than argument-build time, and shellcheck cannot see inside it -- so
every variable an assertion reads looks unused to static analysis while being read on every
run. Each of the 28 read sites was located individually rather than sampled. Every pair named
as suspicious is compared: LCLI298_AGENTS_BASELINE_HASH at :309, CODEX_BRIDGE_HASH_BEFORE and
_AFTER at :271, BEFORE_INDEX and AFTER_INDEX at :1085.

HOW THE WRONG CLAIM GOT IN, which is the part worth keeping: I read shellcheck's output and
the variable NAMES and reasoned from naming convention -- a *_BEFORE/*_AFTER pair with no
visible comparison, a *_RC with no visible check -- then wrote that inference into this
description in the assertive register, where it reached the orchestrator as a finding rather
than a hypothesis. A LINTER'S OUTPUT PLUS AN IDENTIFIER NAME IS NOT EVIDENCE ABOUT BEHAVIOUR:
"unused" is a statement about what the analyser can see, and the whole point of an eval idiom
is that it cannot see. A claim about code I have not opened is a hypothesis and has to be
labelled as one when it leaves the session, not caveated after it lands.

ONE GENUINE FINDING OF THE 29: SPEC_ID (run-e2e.sh:705), assigned from DOC_ID[Spec] and never
read anywhere in the repository. Deleted rather than annotated. Confirmed by the reviewer to
be genuinely unreferenced including inside eval'd assertion strings, and confirmed that
SPEC_PATH -- which looks like its pair -- is read in five places and was correctly left alone.

WHAT SHIPPED
- scripts/lint-shell.sh + `bun run lint:shell`: shellcheck -S warning over git ls-files
  '*.sh', so a new script is covered the moment it is tracked. FAILS rather than skips when
  shellcheck is absent.
- ci.yml runs the identical command, Linux-only.
- steps.sh's SC2148 fixed with `# shellcheck shell=bash`, not a shebang: it is sourced.
- run-e2e.sh carries a file-level SC2034 disable with mechanism, measurement and cost beside
  it. Only executable change to that file is the SPEC_ID deletion -- verified by diffing both
  sides with comments and blanks stripped.
All four tracked .sh files went from 30 findings to zero.

THE REVIEWER PASS FOUND THAT THE GATE DOES NOT GATE, which is the most valuable thing here and
the irony is not lost: a change whose subject is signals that look like enforcement shipped a
step that looks like enforcement and is not. dev's ruleset requires exactly three contexts and
the shell lint runs only in the ubuntu-latest leg, which is none of them -- verified on the
PR's own run, `success` on ubuntu and `skipped` on windows. A PR whose only defect is a
shellcheck finding reddens a non-required job and merges anyway. It cannot move to the windows
leg: that runner image ships no shellcheck (checked against the runner-images manifests --
ubuntu-24.04 and ubuntu-24.04-arm both carry 0.9.0-1, windows carries none).

So the step is now LABELLED advisory, in its own name and in a comment naming the three
required contexts and why this is not one. MAKING IT ENFORCING NEEDS A RULESET CHANGE --
either requiring "lint · typecheck · test (ubuntu-latest)" or giving the shell lint its own
required context -- which is repository governance, not a decision this workflow can make for
itself. RAISED WITH THE ORCHESTRATOR AND STILL OPEN. Until it is resolved this is a report,
not a gate, and it says so rather than being left to be trusted.

TWO MORE REVIEWER FINDINGS, both real. (1) My `set -u` claim was OVERBROAD, and that mattered
because with SC2034 off file-wide it was the only remaining signal for that file: set -u kills
only the shell the bad expansion happens in, so inside a command substitution or subshell the
substitution yields empty and the assertion can pass vacuously. 45 of the 151 check calls here
contain a command substitution. No current assertion has the vacuous form -- checked
exhaustively -- but the comment as written would have taught the next person otherwise.
Narrowed, with the dangerous shape named explicitly. (2) lint-shell.sh REPORTED SUCCESS FOR AN
INSPECTION THAT DID NOT HAPPEN when git failed, which is the exact defect it refuses for a
missing shellcheck. Fixed, and verified with a detached copy outside a repo.

Fixing (2) surfaced a bug of my own that no review caught: `$(git ls-files -z)` does not work
at all, because bash STRIPS NUL from command substitution -- every path concatenated into one
argument. Now read into an array through a temp file, which also keeps git's exit status
checkable where a process substitution would hide it. That also removed the unquoted-glob
hazard the reviewer raised, by construction rather than by narrowing the comment.

RECORDED, NOT FIXED: shellcheck is unpinned and already differs between the keyboard (0.11.0)
and CI (0.9.0), so a local pass is not a proof of a CI pass and a runner-image bump can redden
an unrelated PR. The version is printed on every run so that is diagnosable rather than
mysterious. Pin it if it bites.

The count in the first commit said 31; the baseline on origin/dev is 30 (29 SC2034 + 1
SC2148). The extra was publish-release.sh's SC2088, already fixed by LCLI-486 before this
branch's baseline.

bun run lint 0, lint:shell 0, typecheck 0, 2983 tests pass / 0 fail, lore check 77 files 0
errors 0 warnings.
